newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Feb 13.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Feb 13.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Business Council of Australia is due to launch a plan to recapture its political influence under a Coalition Government, after claims by many members that the organisation had lost its way in the late years of the Labor Government. Page 1

Prime Minister John Howard has denied any wrongdoing by Transport Minister John Sharp and Aboriginal Affairs Minister John Herron, as the Government struggles to regain control of the political agenda in the face of a barrage of allegations of misconduct. Page 1.

The future of the $1 billion RTZ-CRA Century zinc project is expected to be decided today, as the deadline under the right-to-negotiate process provided under the Native Title Act draws close. Tense meetings between the mining company and Aboriginal claiants took place last night in Mt Isa, but some claimants still need to be flown in. Page 2.

The Telstra proposal to charge 50 cents for directory assistance calls has been effectively ruled out by Prime Minister John Howard, who assured Parliament the plan would not be allowed to go ahead if it conflicted with pre-election commitments. Communictions Minister Richard Alston however, said it was too soon to rule out the proposal. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

A Newspoll survey conducted for The Australian has revealed that republicans are far more likely to participate in the Federal Government's People's Convention, and also reveals a dramatic drop in opposition to Australia becoming a republic. The survey shows that those who declare themselves uncommitted to the issue of a republic have increased. Page 1.

Transport Minister John Sharp will today face new allegations about job offers to Civil Aviation Safety Authority board members, after Prime Minister John Howard last night defended his minister. Page 1.

Senator Bob Woods' former lover has withdrawn an apprehended violence order against the senator, averting further publicity for the Liberal Party. Senator Woods failed to appear at the hearing held at the North Sydney Local Court yesterday. Page 1.

Home mortgage rates began to fall yesterday following the announcement by the Commonwealth Bank that it had slashed the price of standard loans by 0.7 percentage points to a 23-year low of 7.55 per cent. The benefits are expected to flow rapidly to all home loan holders. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Sydney Water is to fight a $1 billion private proposal which would see treated effluent recycled into the main water supply, stopping Sydney Harbour's sewage pollution and closing three deep-ocean outfalls. The plan was presented to Minister for Urban Affairs and Planning Tim Knowles by Australian Water Services. Page 1.

North Ryde man Alan Whyman is one of four Australians in a clinical trial of a new treatment which uses the body's immune system to destroy cancerous tumour cells. Fifty patients world wide will be involved in the trial. Page 1.

NSW public health authorities have warned that all livestock industry workers should be vaccinated following the infection of 26 meat-workers at Young with the deadly Q Fever. The virus, described as halfway between a virus and a bacteria, can cause one in 40 who contract the fever to die. Page 1.

The Commonwealth Bank has slashed its standard variable home loan to 7.55 per cent, passing on the benefits from its $602 million half-yearly profit. The move has reignited the mortgage war which has seen borrowers reap huge savings over the past two and half years. Page1.
THE AGE

Prime Minister John Howard has obtained legal advice over allegations that two of his senior Ministers, Transport Minister John Sharp and Aboriginal Affairs Minister John Herron, had breached the Crimes Act by offering jobs to Gabi Hollows in return for her resignation from the board of the Civil Aviation Safety Authority. Page 1.

Mining giant BHP is seeking Federal Government approval for a gas rig 14 kilometres from the Twelve Apostles to take gas from the Minerva field off Port Campbell. BHP said the rig's visual impact would be evaluated in an environmental impact study, and assured the rig would be smaller than others in the area. Page 1.

Research by the San Francisco Cancer Institute has found an anti-cancer virus that infects and kills tumour cells but spares normal cells. Test with human adenovirus found it eliminated 60 per cent of tumours when injected into mice. Page 1.

The Geelong Cats have called for an AFL club summit on the Waverley stadium which is expected to cost between A$14 million and $50 million to modernise. Ticket price rises and reduced club dividends would be the most likely means of raising funds for such a development. Page 1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
